title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos featuring the faces of Dutch celebrities, politicians, and public figures were hosted on a platform accessible to millions of users. The videos were created by digitally manipulating the likenesses of the victims without their consent into sexually explicit material, which is illegal under revenge porn laws in the Netherlands. This represents a failure of content moderation at the platform level, where such material remained accessible despite its clear illegality and harm to identifiable people.

The deployment failure here is systemic: a platform with significant traffic did not prevent the creation, upload, or distribution of illegal sexual imagery. Whether the platform lacked detection capabilities, enforcement mechanisms, or human review of reported content is not established by these reports. What is clear is that victims had to discover the content themselves and pursue individual complaints and legal action rather than the platform removing material proactively.

The incident illustrates how generative technology can be used at scale to commit crimes against identifiable people with few immediate consequences. It took police investigation and prosecution to stop at least one perpetrator. A lawyer's warning that without intervention more fake videos would appear suggests the platform's existing systems were insufficient to deter or prevent ongoing abuse.

summary:
Multiple Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering their faces have been digitally manipulated into pornographic videos. These fake videos appear on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains numerous deepfake pornography videos featuring Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Acting Justice Minister Yesilgöz described the videos as sickening and urged victims to file complaints with police.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore illegal. Managers and representatives of several victims confirmed they have filed reports or are considering legal action. A lawyer warned that without government intervention, more fake pornographic videos featuring celebrities will continue to appear. Victims have several options available, including filing police reports, starting a class action lawsuit, filing complaints with the Data Protection Authority, or contacting hosting companies. One notable case involved television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma, whose deepfake videos led to a 39-year-old man receiving a conditional 180-hour community service sentence in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
